question: Do the public ASEANO Imus pollution outputs establish fish occurrence, and what river, station, salinity, and reuse context can be retained safely?

sourceReviews.title: The situation and causes of plastic pollution in the Imus River, Cavite

findings.scope: The baseline assesses knowledge and plastic practices in Cavite and LGUs along Imus River. It states that a detailed Imus River study had not been conducted as of its 2020 publication.
findings.fishContext: Its fewer-than-20 identified-fish summary concerns nearby Cañas, Pasong Camachile, and Timalan watershed studies; it supplies no fish names or allocation to Imus River or to any single nearby river. A separate 148-metric-ton fish-and-prawn aquaculture figure is for a combined Imus-Ylang-Ylang-Rio Grande water-quality-management area, not a wild-fish inventory.
findings.limitation: The statement about the lack of a detailed Imus study is bounded to the authors' knowledge in 2020 and does not establish that later fish research is absent.

sourceReviews.title: ASEANO project page and report inventory

findings.catalog: The official project page lists the Imus baseline, watershed mapping, plastic-source mapping, knowledge/attitudes/practices, plastic-litter survey, social-implications, and food-service-industry reports, plus a toolkit and end-project proceedings.
findings.fishEvidence: The listed knowledge products are project and pollution-management outputs. Their presence in the inventory does not establish a fish-species inventory or identify the separate CvSU fish-tissue lead mentioned in forum proceedings.
findings.retrievalValue: The catalog establishes a public route to the report set and allows each report to be screened separately; it does not establish that this is the complete output of CvSU's broader biophysical-characterization project.

sourceReviews.title: ASEANO Project Report: Survey on Plastic Litter Along Imus River
sourceReviews.provider: De La Salle University-Dasmariñas; PEMSEA; ASEANO project

findings.studyScope: The 56-page report describes visual and active-trawl surveys of macroplastic litter, water sampling for microplastics, and physicochemical water measurements. It is not a fish survey and reports no fish specimens, species checklist, fish-tissue result, or diet data.
findings.stationContext: The report names upstream, midstream, and downstream barangay locations across Silang, Dasmariñas, Imus, Bacoor, and Kawit. It provides no station coordinates in the reviewed text. Its figures describe eight stations while the station narrative names ten barangay labels; the exact station-count and locality crosswalk remains unresolved, so no points or geometry are inferred.
findings.samplingWindow: The methods describe dry-month sampling in March-April and wet-month sampling in July-August at the same locations; the reviewed methods passage does not specify the calendar year of these sampling events.
findings.historicalSalinity: The report gives a sampled salinity range of 0.12-14.35 ppt and calls the downstream Mabolo/Binakayan and Pulvorista/Sineguelasan locations estuarine/brackish in its study context. These observations are not a current reach-wide salinity classification or safety advisory.
findings.waterQualityBoundary: The report compares physicochemical measurements with the cited Class C criteria and identifies parameters needing monitoring. These historical measurements do not establish present-day water or seafood safety, fishing legality, or access.

sourceReviews.title: End of Project Stakeholders' Forum on the Results of the ASEAN-Norwegian Cooperation Project on Local Capacity Building for Reducing Plastic Pollution in the ASEAN Region (ASEANO Project)
sourceReviews.provider: PEMSEA; Provincial Government Environment and Natural Resources Office, Cavite

findings.separateFishTissueLead: The forum mentions CvSU fish-tissue microplastics research in Bacoor and says results could be shared, but provides no study identity, taxon, site, date, method, dataset, or voucher. The plastic-litter report does not identify itself as that fish-tissue study.

evidenceSynthesis.fishOccurrence: No fish taxa, specimen observations, fish-sampling methods, or occurrence records for Imus River are established by the reviewed ASEANO baseline or plastic-litter survey.
evidenceSynthesis.stationBoundary: Barangay station labels are source-reported research context only. The count/assignment discrepancy and absence of coordinates prevent adopting station points, channel geometry, or a fishing-area boundary.
evidenceSynthesis.salinityBoundary: Preserve only the report's historical, station-specific brackish-water observation. Keep the Imus River scope salinity classification unknown until a current, location-resolved source supports a reach-specific classification.
evidenceSynthesis.otherEvidenceLanes: Plastic pollution, physicochemical water sampling, fish occurrence, fish-tissue microplastics, food safety, and fishing rules are separate evidence lanes. None can substitute for another.

rightsReview.decision: Retain bibliographic metadata and minimal factual findings only. Do not reproduce report tables, maps, figures, raw measurements, or data in the public app without item-specific rights review.

limitations: The baseline's historical statement that no detailed Imus River study existed is limited to its 2020 publication and does not establish that later research does not exist.
The pollution survey is not a fish inventory and does not resolve the separate Bacoor fish-tissue microplastics study mentioned in the forum proceedings.
The report's eight-station figure descriptions and ten named barangay labels were not reconciled; the location table is not sufficient to create coordinates or adopted geometry.
Salinity and physicochemical values are historical study observations with no confirmed current status; they are not safety, seafood, access, or regulatory advice.
No item-specific reuse license for the baseline, project catalog, or plastic-litter survey was verified.

sources.supports: Official ASEANO project report inventory and knowledge-product list.
Official publication metadata, study description, and download link for the DLSU-D Imus River plastic-litter report.
Full report's methods, station names, sampling seasons, plastic and water measurements, and historical downstream brackish-water observations.
Historical Imus baseline's fish-study-gap statement and unassigned nearby-watershed fish summary.
Separate, unidentified CvSU Bacoor fish-tissue microplastics retrieval lead.

queries: "Bio-physical Characterization, Vulnerability and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed"
"microplastics research in fish tissues" Bacoor CvSU
boundedSearch.outcome: The exact broader CvSU project entry is verifiable, but no full final report or fish-specific results were located in this bounded public search. The published ASEANO litter survey is an environmental-pollution output, not the unidentified fish-tissue study. Search failure does not establish that either deliverable or data do not exist.
limits: Search-engine coverage does not include all CvSU library holdings, internal project files, unpublished reports, theses, local-government archives, or records shared privately.
The review is limited to official PEMSEA/CvSU/ASEANO sources and the report text; no external request was sent.

nextAction: Continue public institutional searches for the titled CvSU Bacoor fish-tissue study and the final Imus biophysical-characterization report. Require taxon, exact site/waterbody, sampling date/method, identification or voucher support, and reuse terms before species-level use. Keep historical pollution/salinity results out of current safety advice and preserve the Imus salinity class and geometry as unknown/undelineated.
